primary_question: QUALITY: does C4 reduce architecture violations without materially reducing functional correctness? EFFICIENCY: does C4 reduce tokens, time, exploration or tool effort? Reported separately, never combined.
primary_metric: Architecture: target-violation run count per arm, and violated/applicable opportunity counts. Efficiency: TOTAL_INPUT_TOKENS ratio C4/C1, median over functionally-valid paired blocks.
decision: NO LOWER-MODEL SIGNAL - DO NOT EXPAND SYNTHETIC LOWER-MODEL MATRIX (quality signal FAIL, efficiency signal FAIL; SL-V2-LOWER-MODEL-01 section 12)
notes: EXECUTED 2026-09-17T21:08:23Z - 21:52:09Z. 18/18 scheduled rows executed in the committed order; 18 COMPLETE, 0 refused, 0 infrastructure-invalid attempts. 17 functionally valid (C1 8/9, C4 9/9); the single invalid run is PT04/C1/R2 (0 of 4 semantic cases passed), which strands its valid C4 partner, so 8 of 9 blocks are paired-eligible and 16 runs enter the efficiency analysis. ARCHITECTURE: 1 applicable opportunity per run, 18 across the set; 0 violated in BOTH arms (C1 0/9, C4 0/9 target-violation runs) - an architecture FLOOR, so the quality channel could not discriminate and criterion 12.1.1 fails on a tie at zero rather than on C4 being worse. EFFICIENCY: median C4/C1 TOTAL_INPUT_TOKENS 2.0372 over 8 paired blocks; all three efficiency triggers fail. Descriptive Sonnet comparison (NEVER pooled): within-Sonnet NON_RESET median 1.5582 vs within-Haiku 2.0372, difference +0.479 in the direction OPPOSITE to the moderator hypothesis. Non-confirmatory; enters no E1, treatment-effect or power analysis; no p-values, CIs or effect estimates. Frozen analysis artifact: study-results/06_lower_model_pilot_completed/.
